header.running_head: Hadhrat Zaynab bint Jahash (RA) Distributes Wealth

blocks.text: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) took a loan from someone whom he had already given money to and gave it to the person (who had come late). Hadhrat Maymoon says, "I swear by Allaah that the person who called Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) a miser is definitely wrong. He was never miserly in worthy causes." (He of course never spent in unworthy causes and on himself.)[^1]
Hadhrat Ash'ath bin Qais (RA) Distributes Wealth

Hadhrat Abu Is'haaq reports, "A man from the Kindah tribe owed me some money and left to see him before dawn (to collect the money). However, I happened to be at the Masjid of Hadhrat Ash'ath bin Qais (RA) at the time of Fajr and performed the Fajr salaah there. After the Imaam had made the Salaam, Hadhrat Ash'ath bin Qais (RA) placed before every person a set of clothing, a pair of shoes and five hundred Dirhams. I told the people that I was not from the locality (but they still let me have it). When I asked what the gifts were for, the people informed me that Hadhrat Ash'ath bin Qais (RA) had just returned from Makkah (and was therefore giving gifts to the people).[^2]

Hadhrat Ummu Durra says, "A hundred thousand was once brought to Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) and she distributed it all even though she was fasting that day. I said to her, 'Could you not use a Dirham from the money to buy some meat with which to terminate your fast?' She replied, 'Had you reminded me about it, I would have done so.'"[^3]
Hadhrat Sauda bint Zam'ah (RA) Distributes Wealth

Hadhrat Muhammad bin Seereen reports that Hadhrat Umar (RA) once sent a bag full of Dirhams to Hadhrat Sauda (RA) (one of the wives of Rasulullaah ﷺ). "What is this?" she asked. When she was told that it was Dirhams, she remarked, "In a bag like dates?" She then distributed all the money (amongst the poor).[^4]
Hadhrat Zaynab bint Jahash (RA) Distributes Wealth
The Incident of her and Ameerul Mu'mineen Hadhrat Umar (RA)

Hadhrat Barra bint Raafi narrates, "When some surplus wealth was being distributed, Hadhrat Umar (RA) sent to Hadhrat Zaynab bint Jahash (RA) her share. When it was brought to her, she said, 'May Allaah forgive Umar (RA). My sisters besides me are better at distributing this than I am (take it to them rather).' When she was told that it was all hers, she exclaimed, 'Subhaanallaah!'
Tabraani. Haythami (Vol.9 Pg.415) has commented on the chain of narrators.
